registered_hypothesis: A research architecture can improve system-level research capability by selectively amplifying model strengths, suppressing predictable model failure modes, and explicitly substituting or complementing weak operations with external mechanisms, but only where matched-model ablations show decision-relevant improvement without blocking-validity regressions.
null_hypothesis: Capability-specific scaffolding provides no reliable improvement over the same model with a simpler baseline once task packet, answer contract, evaluator, hidden labels, model configuration, tool/resource budget and cost accounting are controlled.
non_claims: Tool access is equivalent to improved intrinsic model reasoning.
External solver success is evidence that the base model itself became more capable.
Any one workflow should be universally active across cognitive operations.

worlds.purpose: A frozen decomposition scaffold improves task success for the same model and same resources without worsening blocking metrics.
An immutable negative-evidence ledger reduces repeated refuted hypotheses while task quality is non-inferior.
A portfolio search scaffold increases hypothesis coverage and decreases premature-convergence failures under matched budget.
A more complex multi-agent scaffold adds cost but no registered capability gain.
A workflow increases nominal success but worsens a blocking validity metric.
Adding a deterministic solver improves system success; the gain is valid system capability but not pure model-utilization amplification.
The challenger silently receives additional tools or external knowledge.
Baseline and challenger use different base models while claiming workflow-only uplift.
Baseline and challenger are evaluated on different task packets.
The capability-shaping policy is modified after benchmark labels or expected failures are exposed.
A same-context critique pass is described as independent review.
A deterministic verifier catches arithmetic errors the model misses; attribution records substitution rather than intrinsic reasoning gain.
A complex scaffold harms cost/latency on simple tasks without quality improvement.
Atomic decomposition reduces long-horizon constraint-loss errors while preserving output contract and resources.
Structured persistent memory reduces contradiction and forgotten-negative errors relative to chat-context-only memory.
A verifier catches some failures but creates enough false alarms to worsen a blocking validity metric.
The evaluator cannot establish whether the benchmark and operator contract were frozen before results were observed.

evaluation_requirements: Same-model attribution requires identical base-model identity and configuration.
Workflow-only attribution requires the same frozen task packet, answer contract and declared external resources.
Any resource difference must be explicit and changes the attribution class.
Hidden labels and expected outcomes must not be exposed to the operator designer during the frozen trial.
Blocking validity regressions dominate non-blocking gains.
No single scalar may erase cost, validity, failure suppression and task-success tradeoffs.
A capability-shaping operator must name the strength exploited, weakness targeted, compensating mechanism and falsifier.
No support evaluator may activate a default workflow or scientific authority by itself.
promotion_falsifier: If capability-specific shaping does not outperform a simpler matched baseline on at least one registered non-blocking meta-QoI while preserving all blocking meta-QoIs, the operator remains optional/research-only and must not become default behavior.
